hero.lead: A nation of 3.1 million with forest across four tenths of its land, where citizens abroad send home a tenth of the economy and the EU has earmarked €976.6 million under its Growth Plan.

capital.heading: A Growth Plan waiting to pay, and sanitation to build.

register.name: Eurobond of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
register.detail: Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina · completed 28 May 2026 · fixed coupon 5% · its second Eurobond issue
register.note: The IMF records €800 million issued in June 2026, 3.9% of the Federation’s GDP
register.text: The second issue of Eurobonds by the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the international capital market, at a fixed interest rate of 5%. The IMF puts the issue at 3.9% of the Federation’s GDP.

register.name: Benchmark Eurobond of Republika Srpska
register.detail: Ministry of Finance of Republika Srpska · announced 26 March 2026 · fixed coupon 6.25% · matures April 2031
register.note: Demand exceeded €1 billion within a few hours; the IMF records a further €250 million Eurobond placed privately in May 2026
register.text: A €500 million benchmark Eurobond of Republika Srpska with a fixed coupon of 6.25%, maturing in April 2031. Demand exceeded €1 billion within a few hours of the announcement, almost three times that of its inaugural Eurobond issue in 2021.

register.name: Health Systems Improvement Project (P171150), loan of April 2026
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · approved 29 April 2026
register.note: FENA (3 September 2026) reports a €45 million IBRD loan to Republika Srpska for additional financing of the project
register.text: A World Bank loan under the Health Systems Improvement Project, listed by the World Bank with a principal of US$51.6 million. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Sustainable Waste Management Project (SWEEP)
register.detail: World Bank · approved 10 March 2026 · US$54 million equivalent
register.note: Better waste services for over one million people
register.text: A World Bank loan to close and rehabilitate unsanitary dumpsites, upgrade regional sanitary landfills and expand waste separation, recycling, composting and recovery. It improves service quality for over one million people, for the health standard.

register.name: Federation Road Asset Management Enhancement Project
register.detail: World Bank · approved 11 February 2026 · US$80.97 million equivalent · with an €8.5 million EU grant (WBIF)
register.note: About 150 km of priority national roads, the Mostar North junction and safer crossings in about 20 school zones
register.text: A World Bank loan, with an EU grant from the Western Balkans Investment Framework, to rehabilitate or upgrade about 150 kilometres of priority national roads in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and to make roads safer, including in about 20 school zones. It serves the livelihood standard through safer, more reliable connections.

register.name: Second Health Sectors Programmatic Development Policy Loan
register.detail: World Bank · approved 29 January 2025 · P180544
register.note: The second operation in the series that began with the $100 million loan of March 2023
register.text: Budget support for reforms that strengthen the financial sustainability of the health system, by clearing sector arrears and adding governance rules to prevent new ones. It also supports better delivery of health services and preventive care, for the health standard.

register.name: Geospatial Infrastructure and Valuation Enhancement (GIVE)
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 16 May 2024
register.note: €23.1 million approved by the Board on 15 May 2024 for the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as stated by its Federal Administration for Geodetic and Property Affairs
register.text: A World Bank loan to modernise land administration, geospatial infrastructure and property valuation. It bears on the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Sava and Drina Rivers Corridors, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 25 July 2023
register.note: EUR 37 million in the World Bank release of 25 July 2023; about 300,000 people to benefit from better flood protection
register.text: Additional World Bank financing that extends the first phase of the Sava and Drina Rivers Corridors Integrated Development Program to the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Brčko District. About 300,000 people are to benefit from better flood protection, for the shelter standard.

register.name: Air Quality Improvement Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 30 May 2023
register.note: Project page not re-read on 17 November 2026
register.text: A World Bank loan for cleaner air in the most polluted towns. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Health Sectors Programmatic Development Policy Loan
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 20 March 2023
register.note: The second operation of the series, $75 million, was approved on 29 January 2025
register.text: Budget support for health sector reforms, the first loan of a programmatic series. It serves the health standard.

register.name: EU4Employment: skills for green and digital jobs
register.detail: European Union · implemented by the ILO · announced 10 November 2026 · project value €5.5 million
register.note: Grants to ten projects to train at least 1,800 people, and to help at least 600 into work or self-employment
register.text: An EU contribution of €5 million to a €5.5 million project, implemented by the International Labour Organization, that funds ten projects to train and upskill people for green and digital jobs. It focuses on those furthest from the labour market, including young people, rural women, the long-term unemployed, persons with disabilities and Roma, for the education and livelihood standards.

register.name: IPA III 2025–2027 programme: EU grants
register.detail: European Union · Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance · ratification completed 17 August 2026 · non-repayable
register.note: Governance, rule of law, green agenda and connectivity, competitiveness, and agriculture and fisheries
register.text: Non-repayable EU grant funding, unlocked when Bosnia and Herzegovina completed the ratification of the IPA III 2025–2027 programme. It supports climate change mitigation, waste management, competitiveness, climate-resilient farming and food safety, among other reforms and investments, for the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Variable shunt reactors for the transmission grid
register.detail: EBRD · loan of up to €46 million to Elektroprenos-Elektroprijenos BiH (TransCo) · undated at source
register.note: Four variable shunt reactors for key substations across the country
register.text: An EBRD loan to the national electricity transmission company to buy four variable shunt reactors and install them at key substations across the country. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: University of Banja Luka medical education and research campus
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approval announced 19 June 2026
register.note: Brings scattered facilities together, close to the University Clinical Centre
register.text: A Council of Europe Development Bank loan to develop an integrated medical education and research campus at the University of Banja Luka, with energy-efficient buildings for patients, staff and students. It serves the education and health standards.

register.name: Foča–Hum road, on the Sarajevo–Podgorica route
register.detail: EBRD · sovereign loan of up to €60 million approved by the Board 14 May 2026 · co-financed by a €39.4 million World Bank loan · 13.3 km
register.note: The EU provided a €700,000 grant for the feasibility study
register.text: An EBRD loan to Bosnia and Herzegovina to build a new 13.3 km road section from Donji Kopilovi, near Foča, to the Hum border crossing with Montenegro. It strengthens a regional transport corridor, for the livelihood standard.

register.name: Reform and Growth Facility (EU Growth Plan)
register.detail: European Commission · Reform Agenda approved 4 December 2025 · funds released as reforms are carried out
register.note: Pre-financing can start only once the Facility and Loan Agreements enter into force; the IMF baseline assumes €172 million of disbursements in 2026–28
register.text: Grants and concessional loans of up to €976.6 million, released as Bosnia and Herzegovina carries out the reforms of its Reform Agenda. The Commission’s Facility page lists release decisions for Albania, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia only.

register.name: Poklečani wind farm, 132 MW
register.detail: EIB · loan signed in 2025 · expected 437 GWh a year
register.note: With EU grants and technical assistance
register.text: An EIB loan for the 132 MW Poklečani wind farm, expected to generate 437 GWh a year, enough for about 72,700 households, and to cut CO₂ emissions by about 446,900 tonnes a year. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Social impact credit line for SMEs and mid-caps, Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH
register.detail: EIB Global · signed in Sarajevo, 17 December 2025 · with a €3.3 million grant
register.note: EIB Global also advises the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina on green financing
register.text: An EIB Global credit line through Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH to ease financing for small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps, encouraging inclusive employment practices. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Microcredit for rural micro-enterprises and women entrepreneurs, Mikrofin
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approval announced 1 October 2025 · backed by a Social Impact Account guarantee
register.note: At least 60% for micro-enterprises in rural areas and women entrepreneurs
register.text: A Council of Europe Development Bank loan to Mikrofin to expand access to microcredit for underserved communities, for business and farming. It serves the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: Energy-efficiency loans for low-income households, Partner Microcredit Foundation
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 26 January 2024 · programme 2024–2026 · in progress
register.note: The programme reaches €7.5 million with an additional loan
register.text: A Council of Europe Development Bank loan to Partner Microcredit Foundation to part-finance small-scale energy-efficiency investments by low-income households and microenterprises. It serves the shelter standard, as the programme improves the comfort of dwellings and reduces the burden of energy bills.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 12.8% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

enterprises.heading: Already working in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

items.name: Partner Microcredit Foundation
items.text: A microfinance foundation that lends to low-income households and microenterprises for small-scale energy-efficiency works such as insulation, double-glazed windows and new heating systems, under a programme for 2024 to 2026 that aims to make homes more comfortable and energy bills lighter.

items.name: Insieme cooperative
items.text: A cooperative in Bratunac, near Srebrenica, that turns berries into fresh fruit packs, jams and juices, also sold in Italy. In 2024 it counted about 50 member families and 350 supplier families, and 80% of its workers were women.

items.name: Bosnian Handicrafts (BHcrafts)
items.text: A Tuzla-based enterprise, begun in 1995 as a humanitarian project, that trains and employs women, many displaced by the war, to make knitted, crocheted and embroidered goods sold at home and abroad. It employs 500 women from different religious and ethnic groups, and product sales finance 89% of its operations.

items.name: Muharem Berbić Friends Club
items.text: A social business of the Muharem Berbić Foundation in Kakanj that turned a 1936 industrial building into a coffee shop, hall and workshop. It employs people with disabilities, uses its whole profit for their salaries and sources food from rural women.

items.name: Mikrofin
items.text: A microfinance lender in Banja Luka, described by the EBRD as the largest in the country, that offers micro-loans for business and farming. A loan approved by the Council of Europe Development Bank in 2025 expands its microcredit, with at least 60% for micro-enterprises in rural areas and women entrepreneurs.
